<!-- pr-reviewer: 49d0a3c2cb9675a22c2e0682bd7db1d12f00d322 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** The metric G76 is right and well pinned. The inch G76 still makes the control cut one more pass than was verified, and the inch golden this PR changes locks that in.

### What looks good
- Correct reading of the word. `R` is written in the **first** block (`G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)`), so it is the finishing allowance, not the second block's taper `R(i)`. The second block still has no `R`, so the taper stays 0.
- Public lathe references give the same meaning: the first-block `R` is the finish allowance and takes a decimal point; `Q`/`P` take no decimal point and are in least increments; the second-block `Q` is the first pass's depth. With `R0`, the control roughs 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 and then finishes at 1.2 again, which is a fourth pass nobody verified. With `R0.4` it cuts 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2, the three passes that were judged.
- Units agree with each other in both programs. mm: `Q400` (whole µm) and `R0.4` (decimal mm). inch: `Q157` (0.0001 in, so 0.0157 in) and `R0.0157` (decimal in). Converted, both are 0.4 mm.
- The new record `finish_allowance` is the laid finishing pass's own depth (`thread_cycle.rs:59-66`). It cannot panic: `i - 1` is only reached with `i >= 1`. Alternating infeed and one-pass threads are refused by name. The `ALT` word is optional in the stream and in the file, so old streams and projects read back to the same bytes.
- The Tormach lathe goldens are byte-identical to main (I checked `tormach-lathe/thread_g76_mm.nc` and `thread_g76_inch.nc`). No other dialect has a G76 golden. Only the Fanuc-lathe goldens changed: `thread_g76.nc` (mm and inch) and the new `thread_g76_area.nc`.
- Hygiene: no process files, no `PROCESS_VERSION` edit, no `CHANGELOG.md` edit, no snapshot PNGs. `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #417` are present, and the subjects are conventional. New code has no `unwrap`/`expect`.

### Local results (head 49d0a3c2, already contains `upstream/main` f2b42e3d, so the trial merge was a no-op)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| app `lathe_post` | 7 passed |
| app `lathe_post_inch` | 6 passed |
| app `lathe_post_g76` | 8 passed |
| app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` | 4 passed |
| app `lathe_post_tormach` / `lathe_post_tormach_thread` | 8 / 8 passed |
| app `turning_thread` / `turning_thread_infeed` / `thread_passes` | 10 / 4 / 5 passed |
| app `golden_cl` / `project_roundtrip` / `recorded_post_streams` / `posting` | 32 / 73 / 5 / 17 passed |
| camcraft-post (all suites) | 464 passed, 0 failed |
| camcraft-cl (all suites) | 49 passed, 0 failed |
| motion `turning_thread` / `turning_thread_cycle` / `turning_thread_infeed` / lib | 18 / 3 / 8 / 328 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Mutation checks** (`fanuc-lathe.cps` and `thread_cycle.rs`, reverted after each run):
| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| `R` forced to 0 | g76, inch, schedule |
| `R` not converted to inch | inch |
| `R` written as a no-point increment (`R400`/`R157`) | g76, inch, schedule |
| inch `R` at 3 decimals (`R0.016`) | inch |
| `R` = first depth instead of the finishing step | schedule only (the default thread has equal values) |
| record finish = plan allowance (old behaviour) | g76, schedule, motion `turning_thread_cycle` |
| Fanuc alternating refusal removed | schedule |
| one-pass refusal removed | schedule |

### Requested before merge
1. **The inch G76 words do not describe the three verified passes.** See `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc:12` and `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps:858`. Each word is rounded to its own lattice on its own: `Q`/`P` with `incr()` to 0.0001 in, and `R` with `fu()` to 4 decimals. The control then works on the rounded words. Running this PR's own control model (`control_depths` in `lathe_post_g76_schedule.rs`) on the inch golden words `G76 P010000 Q157 R0.0157` / `G76 X0.378 Z0.315 P472 Q157`:
   ```
   k - d = 0.0472 - 0.0157 = 0.0315
   pass 1: 0.0157
   pass 2: max(0.0157*sqrt2, 0.0157 + 0.0157) = 0.0314   (< 0.0315, not clamped)
   pass 3: max(0.0157*sqrt3, 0.0314 + 0.0157) = 0.0471 -> clamped to k - d = 0.0315
   finish: 0.0472
   control: [0.0157, 0.0314, 0.0315, 0.0472]   laid/verified: 3 passes
   ```
   That is four passes instead of three: a 0.0001 in rub pass that was never verified. It does not gouge, but it is the same kind of mismatch #417 is meant to remove, and it is on a golden this PR edits. (Main's `R0` gives five passes, so this is an improvement, but not yet the claim.) `R0.0158` would give exactly `[0.0157, 0.0314, 0.0472]`.
   Suggested fix: in `onThreadCycle`, work out the control's ladder from the **rounded** words (`incr(FirstDepth)`, `incr(MinimumDepth)`, `incr(ThreadHeight)`) and write `R` as `k_w - (last rung)`. Refuse by name if that rung is more than one least increment from the record's `height - finish_allowance`. Pin it with an inch twin of `same_ladder`: `the_default_thread_g76_states_its_three_passes` run under `units(.., "inch")`, which today would fail on the pass count. The same rounding can happen in mm wherever a rung is off the µm lattice, so the check belongs in the post, not just in the inch test.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- A project saved before this PR with a cached thread toolpath keeps `finish_allowance: 0` in its cached record. It posts the old `R0` (one extra root pass) until the operation is regenerated. Is that acceptable, or should the stamp move so the cache shows stale?
- The flank-infeed Z sign and the end-Z shift (body "Not exercised" 1-2) remain unconfirmed from public sources. I agree neither changes the final form for a single-start thread. A Hub or real-control check of `thread_g76_area.nc` before the cut would settle it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: be4546ca0c6d5a942a2295d48e9f9f1465b84c87 -->
This is a full independent review of head `be4546ca`. I did not write any of this PR.

**Needs changes before merge.** The code is clean and the tests pass. The change requested is in the text only: the PR body and the decision file make a safety claim that the sources do not support, and they disagree with each other. The maintainer hold ("stays a draft for the Fanuc-lathe check") is not part of this verdict.

### What looks good
- The Fanuc two-block form is correct for public Fanuc-compatible references. First block `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)`: `m` = finishing repeats (1 + spring passes), `r` = 10 x pull-out / lead, `a` = tool angle. `R` is the finishing allowance. The second block has `X Z P(k) Q(dd) F` and no `R(i)`, so the taper stays 0.
- Units are consistent. mm: `Q`, `P` are whole microns with no decimal point (`Q400`, `P1200`). `R` has a decimal point in mm (`R0.4`). Inch: `Q157`, `P472` are 0.0001 in. `R0.0158` has a decimal point, in inches.
- The `R0.0158` reasoning is sound. 0.4 mm = 0.015748 in. The control reads Q157, P472. Its rough rungs are 157, 314, 471 (clamped to the minimum step). `R0.0157` puts the last rough depth at 315, one increment past rung 2 (314). That gives a fourth, unverified pass. `R0.0158` puts it at 314, so the control cuts 0.0157 / 0.0314 / 0.0472: the verified three passes.
- The refusal is present and named: `fanuc-lathe.cps` `g76Allowance` refuses when R is more than one least increment from the record's allowance. It names the Q, Q and P words and the R window. `a_ladder_the_rounded_words_cannot_state_is_refused_by_name` pins it with 2- and 4-increment records. The same record posts in mm.
- Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` writes the two-block R. The Tormach goldens are byte-identical to main. The default Tormach words (`J K R1`) did not change.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the new Rust. `thread_cycle.rs` reaches `i - 1` only with `i >= 1`. The `ALT` word in `cnc_thread.rs` is optional (absent reads 0), so old streams keep their bytes. `ThreadCycleDto.alternating` is `serde(default)` and written only when set. No new `camcraft-*` dependency, no `PROCESS_VERSION` edit, no process file, no snapshot PNG, no `CHANGELOG.md` edit. Provenance lines are present. New Rust files are under 400 lines (`fanuc-lathe.cps` is a post script, exempt). `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #417` are present. The new test file sits in `crates/app/tests` and its Gate map names the app and motion modules it covers.
- The earlier `needs-rework` point (inch `R0.0157` gave a fourth pass) is answered by `0bb37ddd` with the pin tests above. The non-blocking question about old projects is answered too (see Notes).

### Results merged with main (local, worktree at this head; main `db091cb38` is already merged in, no hand edits)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| app `lathe_post_g76` | 8 passed |
| app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` | 6 passed |
| app `lathe_post_inch` | 6 passed |
| app `lathe_post_tormach_thread` | 8 passed |
| app `thread_passes` | 5 passed |
| app `recorded_post_streams` | 5 passed |
| motion `turning_thread_cycle` | 3 passed |
| `camcraft-post` all suites | 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Not run by me: the other lathe, motion, cl and app suites that the takeover agent lists as green; sim, geometry, kernel, tools and ui suites (not touched). No Fanuc control or simulator run exists for any reading below.

### Requested before merge
1. **Correct the safety claim about the unproven readings**, in the PR body ("Not exercised" 1-2, and "None of these moves the finished thread form") and in `docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`. The text says "either sign is gouge-safe" and "none moves the finished form". The sources do not show that, for a flank (a not 0) thread:
   - Z shift per pass (item 1): the post sets the start Z to `c_first - k*tan(a/2)` and relies on pass n starting at `start + depth_n*tan(a/2)`. If the control shifts the other way, or if the finishing pass sits at the programmed start Z (the reading that matches some Fanuc figures), the whole thread lands off by `k*tan(a/2)` to `2*k*tan(a/2)`. For the new golden that is 0.6 to 1.25 mm on a 2 mm lead. That is a wrong cut position, not a profile detail.
   - End Z (item 2): if the control also shifts each pass's end by `depth*tan(a/2)`, the root pass ends `k*tan(a/2)` past `EndZ`. Where the thread ends at a shoulder, that can cut into the shoulder.

   Please state both as "can move the thread axially, or into a shoulder, on a flank thread; unproven without a Fanuc run". The default radial thread (a = 0, the posted default) is not affected by items 1 and 2. This risk already exists on main for flank threads (#416 posts the angle and the start); this PR does not add it, but its text must not call it safe.
2. **Make the body and the decision file agree.** Differences:
   - Body item 4 says rounding is "handled now". The decision file says single rungs of a long sqrt ladder can still differ by a few increments. Use the decision file's wording in both.
   - Body item 3 (minimum-depth clamp reading) is not in the decision file's list of unverified readings. Add it there.
   - The body says "Hub run: not needed". The decision file says the readings stay open for a run on a Fanuc control. State the same in both.
   - The body carries older lines ("Takeover refresh at 49d0a3c2 ... `R0.0157`") that the head contradicts. Mark them as superseded.

   The body edit needs no push. The decision file needs one plain commit on this branch.

### Judgement of the four unproven items
| Item | Can a wrong reading make a wrong cut? |
|---|---|
| 1. Z-shift sign / which pass sits at the programmed Z | Yes, for flank threads only: thread shifted axially by up to `2*k*tan(a/2)`. Radial default: no effect. |
| 2. End-Z shift | Possible: root pass overruns `EndZ` by `k*tan(a/2)` if the control shifts the end. Shoulder risk. Radial default: no effect. |
| 3. Minimum-depth clamp | Changes pass count or per-pass depth only, never the root. A different clamp can give fewer, deeper passes than verified (load not judged). Equal-depth ladders (the default) are not affected. |
| 4. Rounding | Pass count is fixed by construction. Single rungs of a long sqrt ladder may drift a few microns. Not a gouge. |

Also open at the boundary: the chosen `R` puts the last rough depth exactly on a rung (the mm default too). A control that tests "reached" differently could repeat that rung. That is at most a pass at an already verified depth, so it is safe.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- Old projects: an operation cached before this PR has `finish_allowance` 0. The stamp has no generator version, so it reads Fresh. The Fanuc post then writes `R0` (same as main today): one extra root pass, not a gouge. I confirmed this in `g76Allowance` (f = 0 gives d = 0). The Tormach post is different: `tormach-lathe.cps` now refuses a stale record with allowance 0 (it expects the ladder's last step). A Tormach G76 job therefore refuses by name until the operation is regenerated. That is safe, but the message does not say "regenerate". Suggest a follow-up issue (P7): a generator version in the stamp, or a "regenerate" hint in that refusal.
- `R0.4` replaces `R0` for the default Fanuc G76 thread. This changes posted output, and the decision file records the choice. Please confirm that no `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer is needed. I judge it is not, because the old output cut an unverified pass.
- Some Fanuc parameter settings read a word with no decimal point as least increments. The post follows the existing convention of the file (integer words such as `Z14`). This is an existing assumption of the whole file, not new here.
- #1619 (Tormach inch J/K pass count) is open and covers the known gap on that dialect.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 5c23149d6b2fd64395882fd530ddd5db77d91d50 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

This is a review of the text-only commit after `be4546ca0`. It relies on the full review of `be4546ca0` for code and tests. This head is not built.

**Checks**
- `git diff be4546ca0..5c23149d6` changes one file: `docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`. No code, test or golden changed.
- The four text blockers are answered. The decision file and the PR body both state what a wrong reading can do:
  1. Z-shift sign and which pass sits at the programmed Z: the thread can move axially by `k·tan(a/2)` to `2k·tan(a/2)`.
  2. End-Z shift: the root pass can end past the end Z and cut into a shoulder.
  3. Minimum-depth clamp: only the pass count or the per-pass depth changes, never the root.
  4. Rounding: the pass count is fixed. Single rungs can differ by a few increments. This is not a gouge.
- Both texts say that items 1 and 2 can move a flank thread axially or into a shoulder. Both say these items stay unproven without a Fanuc control run. Both say the default radial thread (a = 0) is not affected.
- The two texts agree with each other and with the code readings.
- The body and the decision file write `R0.0158`. `R0.0157` appears only where it is marked as superseded or as the dropped option.
- The body has a `Changelog:` line and ends with the closing line for #417.
- #1842 (Fanuc control run, P3, with the open question about a refusal or warning for flank G76) and #1843 (Tormach refusal message for a record cached before this PR) exist and are open. Their content is sensible and matches the notes of the full review.
- The PR is `MERGEABLE` with `main`.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The decision file says "the follow-up issue is named in the PR body" and gives no number. The body names #1842. A number in the file would help a later reader.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
